# 01 Viewport module: mouse drag-to-pan, wheel-to-zoom, resetView()

## Outcome

A board created via `createBoard` supports mouse drag-to-pan and cursor-anchored wheel-to-zoom out
of the box, clamped per the spec's rules, with a new `board.resetView()` method that snaps back to
the initial fit-to-container state. The error banner is unaffected by pan/zoom. No control-bar UI
yet (ticket 02) — this ticket's observable behavior is proven through `createBoard`/`Board`'s own
test suite, driving real `MouseEvent`/`WheelEvent` sequences and calling `resetView()` directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `createBoard` restructures its mount so the rendered SVG lives inside a new
      `.siren-board-viewport` element (a new `viewport.ts` module's `content`), itself inside the
      existing `.siren-board-canvas`; the error banner (`.siren-board-error`) stays a direct child
      of `.siren-board-canvas`, a sibling of `.siren-board-viewport`, not inside it.
- [ ] A `mousedown` + `mousemove` sequence over the board's canvas pans the diagram: the
      `.siren-board-viewport` element's applied transform offset changes by the drag delta (scaled
      appropriately by current zoom). A `mouseup` (dispatched on `window`) stops the pan; further
      `mousemove` on `window` without an active drag has no effect.
- [ ] A `wheel` event over the board's canvas changes the applied zoom scale; the point under the
      cursor before the wheel event remains under the cursor after it (cursor-anchored zoom).
      `preventDefault()` is called on the wheel event (verify via a spy) so the host page doesn't
      scroll.
- [ ] Zoom is clamped: repeated zoom-in wheel events never push scale above 4.0x; repeated zoom-out
      wheel events never push scale below 0.1x.
- [ ] Pan is clamped per the spec's two-part rule (test with a stubbed `getBoundingClientRect()`
      giving the canvas a known size): dragging far in one direction cannot move the scaled
      content's edge past the container's opposite edge when content is larger than the container
      on that axis; when zoomed out so scaled content is smaller than the container on an axis,
      drag deltas on that axis produce no offset change (locked centered).
- [ ] `board.resetView()` sets scale back to 1.0 and offset back to (0, 0), regardless of the
      current pan/zoom state reached via drag/wheel.
- [ ] A successful `board.setSource(...)` call resets the view to the initial fit-to-container state
      (same effect as `resetView()`); a `setSource` call that fails to parse/build (previous diagram
      + error banner shown) leaves the current pan/zoom state unchanged.
- [ ] `board.destroy()` removes the viewport's `mousedown`/`wheel` listeners on the canvas and any
      `window`-level `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners left over from an in-progress drag, along with
      its DOM. Calling `destroy()` a second time does not throw.

## Test seam

`createBoard`/`Board` (the package's public interface) — integration tests under jsdom, per the
package's existing convention (see `createBoard.test.ts`). Stub `getBoundingClientRect()` on the
relevant container element via `vi.spyOn` to give tests a controlled size (jsdom returns an
all-zero rect by default). Dispatch real `MouseEvent`/`WheelEvent` instances. Do not add a
`viewport.test.ts` — `viewport.ts` is exercised only through `createBoard`/`Board`, matching
`defaultControls.ts`'s existing precedent of having no test file of its own.
